# Independent TES4 conformance vectors

These 26 project-authored wire vectors are CC0-1.0. Their Java generator and tests
remain Apache-2.0. This separate corpus preserves the original synthetic corpus
and its registered generator identity. No Reference Snapshot source was copied,
and no Oracle execution supplied the generated bytes.

`manifest.json` records each recipe's provenance, exact text digest, decoded wire
digest and length. `generator.json` carries the deterministic recipe inventory.
Every `artifacts/*.hex` contains lowercase hexadecimal followed by LF; decode it
before passing it to an archive API. The generator accepts only absent or empty
output directories:

```powershell
java -cp jbsa-test-support/target/classes io.github.evildarkarchon/jbsa/fixtures/BsaCv1FixtureGenerator --output target/bsa067-corpus
```

All base archives contain `meshes\a.nif` (1024 ASCII `A` bytes) followed by
`meshes\b.nif` (`00 01 02 ff`). Zlib streams use explicit literal DEFLATE blocks,
making their bytes independent of a compression provider. Mixed archives store
the second entry. The three unsupported codec vectors place valid raw DEFLATE,
raw LZ4 or LZ4 frame bytes inside TES4's compressed record framing; readers must
reject them because TES4 requires RFC 1950 zlib.

The malformed inventory includes rejected structure/payloads and structurally
usable inputs whose safe handling must be observed separately:

| Recipes | Intended observation |
| --- | --- |
| arithmetic-overflow, impossible-counts, out-of-range-spans, partial-overlap, truncated-spans, equal-name-identities | Reject invalid structure |
| decompression-mismatch | Reject at complete payload read |
| illegal-tuples | Reject unknown version 0x66 |
| exact-shared-spans | Both entries decode to the first payload |
| harmless-trailing-bytes, ignorable-constants | Preserve readable entries |
| missing-name-tables | Preserve hashes and distinct unresolved names |
| usable-name-hash-mismatch, owning-dispositions | Retain a noncanonical assessment and hash warning |
| undecodable-wire-names | Preserve raw bytes and an unresolved identity with a warning |
| unsafe-absolute-names, unsafe-traversal-names, windows-invalid-names | Permit structural inspection; extraction checks destination eligibility |
| unsafe-name-extraction | Reject traversal extraction without publishing an escaped file |
| xml | Preserve XML's contribution to file flags |

`BsaFixtureCorpusIT` checks exact payloads through public archive operations,
rejection of representative faulty vectors, and deterministic reproduction of
all generator-owned files. The manifest schemas retain the existing corpus
contract. The legacy corpus audit additionally demands accepted goldens, so its
nonempty-golden gate does not apply to this fixture-only preparation step.

The base `goldens` array and index are empty. These vectors alone do not approve
goldens or activate CV1 cases. Any proposed golden manifest and observations are
review artifacts with their own approval lifecycle.
